tool.name: create_vulnerability_report
tool.description:
Create a vulnerability report for a discovered security issue.
Use this tool to document a specific verified security vulnerability. Put ALL details in the content field - affected URLs, parameters, proof of concept, remediation steps, CVE references, CVSS scores, technical details, impact assessment, etc.
DO NOT USE: - For general security observations without specific vulnerabilities - When you don't have concrete vulnerability details - When you don't have a proof of concept, or still not 100% sure if it's a vulnerability - For tracking multiple vulnerabilities (create separate reports) - For reporting multiple vulnerabilities at once. Use a separate create_vulnerability_report for each vulnerability.

parameter.name: title
parameter.description: Clear, concise title of the vulnerability

parameter.name: content
parameter.description: Complete vulnerability details including affected URLs, technical details, impact, proof of concept, remediation steps, and any relevant references. Be comprehensive and include everything relevant.

parameter.name: severity
parameter.description: Severity level: critical, high, medium, low, or info

returns.description: Response containing success status and message

tool.name: create_bug_report
tool.description:
Create a bug report for a discovered QA issue (non-security).
Use this tool to document functional bugs, UI/UX issues, integration failures, or any other quality issues found during testing. Put ALL details in the content field - affected pages/endpoints, environment details, reproduction steps, expected vs actual behavior, screenshots description, frequency, etc.
USE FOR: - Functional bugs (features not working as expected) - UI/UX issues (layout problems, confusing interfaces, accessibility issues) - Integration failures (data not syncing, API contract violations) - Edge case failures (boundary conditions, special characters handling) - Performance issues (slow responses, timeouts) - Data integrity issues (incorrect calculations, data loss) - Error handling issues (poor error messages, unhandled exceptions)
DO NOT USE: - For security vulnerabilities (use create_vulnerability_report instead) - When you're not sure if it's actually a bug - For multiple bugs at once (create separate reports)

parameter.name: title
parameter.description: Clear, descriptive title of the bug

parameter.name: content
parameter.description: Complete bug details including: environment (browser, OS, viewport), preconditions, step-by-step reproduction instructions, expected behavior, actual behavior, evidence/screenshots description, and frequency (always/intermittent/rare). Be comprehensive.

parameter.name: severity
parameter.description: Severity level: blocker (system unusable), critical (major feature broken), major (significant impact), minor (minor inconvenience), or trivial (cosmetic)

returns.description: Response containing success status and message
